Loss of power would immediately shut down all electric motors on the site including compressors, air coolers, and transfer / loading pumps. All operations would cease until power was restored. The Control and Safety system itself would remain on-line, powered by Page83 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version an Uninterruptible Power System (UPS) allowing the operators an opportunity to monitor the plant and initiate any control activities. As pressure is lost from the air system actuated valves would fail to a pre-determined safe state (open, closed, or as is) and pressure increases due to CO product boil-off managed through a network of 2 mechanical relief devices. Should the power be lost during loading or unloading operations these operations would cease at that time. 4.7.6 PRESSURIZED / UN-PRESSURIZED RESTART Following a short shutdown, the liquefaction trains would retain liquid content and chilled CO vapor. A 2 restart from this condition is straightforward and will involve starting individual compressor stages in recycle mode and gradually bringing the incoming gas pipeline on-line once pressures are established and ramping up production. Should the majority of the inventory be lost due to evaporation, it will be necessary to re-establish inventory, pressures, and chill the plant in a controlled manner. This procedure will largely reflect the original plant start up sequence which will be developed along with other operating processes later in design. 4.7.7 LOADING OF EMPTY, AIR FILLED TANKS Periodically, tanks will require inspection resulting in the scenario of having to introduce cold liquid CO 2 into a storage tank filled with warm and humid ambient air. The main concern is humidity in the ambient air introducing water into the tanks and resulting in ice and / or corrosion when the LCO is ultimately 2 introduced. The steps below address the issue. Step 1. Dry Air Flush The first step in the process involves introducing dry instrument air, with a dew point of less than -40 °C, into the tank(s). This effectively replaces the humid ambient air, allowing it to be vented to the atmosphere. Assuming a purging rate that is three times the tank volume, it will take approximately 4.6 hours to dry air purge a single storage tank with a diameter of 10 meters and a length of 32.3 meters. In total, it will take about 2.5 days to dry air purge all 11 storage tanks. This air flush will require the standby air compressor and dryer to be in operation. Step 2. CO Gas Flush 2 The second step involves routing dry CO into the tanks to displace the instrument air. This CO could 2 2 come from storage or the incoming pipeline (depending on which tanks are being purged and the quality of the pipeline gas).
